new_scholarship.name: NTU-University Scholars Programme (NTU-USP) Scholarship
new_scholarship.program_type: University merit scholarship (separate scholarship application submitted immediately after the undergraduate admission application; tenable only by students admitted to the NTU-University Scholars Programme, a Signature Programme of the NTU Honours College)
new_scholarship.official_source: Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Office of Admissions
new_scholarship.duration: Covers up to the normal programme duration of the full-time undergraduate degree programme entered, on condition that the scholarship holder maintains a record of good academic performance and exemplary conduct
new_scholarship.deadline: NTU states "The same application period for admissions applies" and that the scholarship online application deadline is the same as the admission deadline. NTU publishes exact calendar deadlines per admission qualification route for the current (2027 entry) cycle: NUS High School Diploma - scholarship online application by 20 January 2027; Diploma awarded by a polytechnic in Singapore - by 21 February 2027; Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level and IB Diploma - by 19 March 2027. Applicants with Year 12 equivalent qualifications must apply before the application closing date for that qualification, which falls between 15 October 2026 and 19 March 2027.
new_scholarship.application_period: The scholarship application period is exactly the NTU undergraduate admission application period for the applicant's qualification, and NTU requires the admission application to be submitted before the scholarship application. For the current cycle NTU publishes: IB Diploma and most international / Year 12 equivalent qualifications, 15 October 2026 to 19 March 2027 (some Year 12 routes close 20 January 2027); NUS High School Diploma, 1 December 2026 to 20 January 2027; Diploma awarded by a polytechnic in Singapore, 1 to 21 February 2027; Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, day of A-Level results release to 19 March 2027. After submitting the scholarship application, a passport-size photograph and the online appraisal form must follow, by 26 March 2027 (GCE A-Level and IB Diploma routes), 28 February 2027 (polytechnic diploma route) or 27 January 2027 (NUS High School Diploma route).
application_method: This is a SEPARATE scholarship application. It is not automatic on admission and does not replace the undergraduate admission application. NTU states: "Applicants are required to submit their application for admission before submitting their application for scholarship."
First complete the NTU undergraduate admission application through the official Applicant Portal.

Then click the 'Apply for Scholarship' link at the end of the online admission application and log in with the NTU application number (the same password created during the admission application). Applicants with a reserved place log in directly at https://wis.ntu.edu.sg/ords/apex/r/scholarship/scholarship/logins?session.

As part of completing the form, write a Personal Essay of not more than 250 words on the one compulsory topic provided. Applicants also list their top three personal achievements in merit order, drawn from within the last five years.

After submitting, upload a recent passport-size photograph (digital image) and send the referee URL to a school teacher who is not a family member or relative; the referee must submit the online appraisal within 7 days of the scholarship application (preferably not more than 2 weeks). Only one appraisal may be submitted online to support an application.

Applicants with Year 12 equivalent results apply at https://wis.ntu.edu.sg/pls/webexe/adm_fore_appl.login using the assigned application number before the application closing date for that qualification.
Shortlisted applicants attend a scholarship selection interview, in person or online. The scholarship outcome is notified after the interview; NTU states the scholarship outcome decision is final.
Accept the NTU admission offer and the scholarship offer by the stipulated deadline. Only one scholarship may be accepted at any given time.
new_scholarship.description: The NTU-University Scholars Programme (NTU-USP) Scholarship is an NTU merit scholarship for outstanding freshmen admitted to the NTU-University Scholars Programme, a multidisciplinary Signature Programme of the NTU Honours College. It is open to all nationalities and covers full subsidised tuition fees after the Tuition Grant, together with a living allowance, accommodation allowance, computer allowance and a travel grant. The scholarship carries no bond of its own apart from the three-year bond applicable under the MOE Tuition Grant Scheme.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Applicants with outstanding academic results (Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, Singapore polytechnic diploma, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent) combined with excellent co-curricular records and strong leadership potential, who are admitted to a full-time NTU undergraduate degree on the NTU-University Scholars Programme and want a fully funded degree with a semester abroad and broad interdisciplinary study.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to all nationalities. Awardees must be on the NTU-University Scholars Programme (NTU-USP), a Signature Programme of the NTU Honours College, alongside a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NTU. Applicants must hold outstanding academic achievements in the Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, a Diploma awarded by a polytechnic in Singapore, the NUS High School Diploma, the IB Diploma, or a Year 12 equivalent qualification, and must demonstrate excellent co-curricular records and strong leadership qualities and potential. No separate English test, minimum entry GPA or age condition is published for the scholarship itself; renewal requires a minimum CGPA of 3.5 over 5.0.
eligibility: Successful awardees should be on the NTU-University Scholars Programme (NTU-USP).
Successful awardees should be enrolled in a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NTU.

Possess outstanding academic achievements in the Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, Diploma awarded by a polytechnic in Singapore, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent qualifications.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: No published weighting or scoring rubric applies to this scholarship. NTU states that for its scholarships it considers co-curricular activities and leadership qualities alongside academic performance, and that the scholarship selection committee reviews the application and considers the applicant for the best eligible scholarship available based on merit. NTU publishes no separate score threshold. Applicants with Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, Singapore polytechnic diploma, NUS High School Diploma and IB Diploma qualifications attend a selection interview between March and May; only shortlisted applicants are notified by email, by mid-May. Applicants with Year 12 equivalent qualifications are interviewed within 2 months of the NTU programme offer release and notified within a month of the offer date. There is no fee to apply.
new_scholarship.notes: No scholarship bond is attached to this award by NTU itself; the only service obligation is the three-year MOE Tuition Grant bond that applies to all Singapore Permanent Residents and international students who take up the Tuition Grant. 'Full coverage of subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant)' means the subsidised fee, not the non-subsidised fee: the differential for international students and Singapore PRs is not covered, whereas Singapore Citizens pay the subsidised fee only. The accommodation allowance applies only to scholarship holders who reside in NTU hostels. NTU states the scholarship is only valid if an international student or Singapore PR takes up the MOE Tuition Grant. NTU also states allowances are credited for Semester 1 and Semester 2 only, not for vacation or special terms, and that fees for programmes outside Semesters 1 and 2 such as GEM Discoverer are not covered. The research brief named two targets; only one record fits this slot. No award named 'Nanyang President's Undergraduate Scholarship' is published on ntu.edu.sg (a direct probe of that detail-page slug returns HTTP 404). NTU currently publishes the 'NTU President Award', whose stated criteria match that description (open to all nationalities, full-time undergraduate degree, outstanding academic results, excellent co-curricular records, exceptional leadership qualities) and which the AY2026-27 NTU Scholarships brochure marks as a 'New Award' - so it is plausibly the successor award, but NTU does not state a rename and this is an inference, not a verified fact. The NTU-University Scholars Programme (NTU-USP) Scholarship was recorded because it is the primary target named for this slot, is open to all nationalities, and publishes complete benefit figures. The NTU-USP Scholarship benefit figures were cross-checked against the NTU Scholarships brochure (Information correct as at August 2026), which lists identical amounts for this award.

NTU also states the scholarship is only valid if an international student or Singapore PR takes up the MOE Tuition Grant.

programme_detail_official.english_requirement_note: The NTU-USP Scholarship award page publishes no English-language test requirement for the scholarship, and there is no separate English test or score to apply for the scholarship. Separately, NTU's undergraduate admission requirements publish English language proficiency scores that applicants from selected high school qualifications must submit by the deadline of their application window (IELTS Academic or IELTS UKVI Academic overall 6.5 with Writing 6.5 and Speaking 6.5; TOEFL or TOEFL iBT Home Edition total 90 with Writing 25 and Verbal/Speaking 25). Those are admission entry requirements rather than scholarship requirements, so no score is recorded as a scholarship requirement here.
selection_criteria: Outstanding academic achievements in an accepted qualification route.
Co-curricular activities and leadership qualities are considered alongside academic performance.
Selection interview: only shortlisted applicants are notified by email and invited to an interview.
programme_detail_official.duration: Covers up to the normal programme duration of the full-time undergraduate degree programme entered, conditional on a record of good academic performance and exemplary conduct.
award_holder_conditions: Scholarship holder must not, without the approval of the University, hold concurrently any other scholarships, bursaries, university loans or awards.
Scholarship holder is required to maintain a minimum Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 3.5 over 5.0. Academic performance will be reviewed every semester.
The scholarship may be withdrawn at any time if, in the opinion of the University, the scholarship holder's progress or behaviour is deemed unsatisfactory.
If the scholarship holder decides to terminate the scholarship prematurely, a repayment will be imposed.
No bond is attached to the NTU-USP Scholarship apart from the three-year bond applicable to all Singapore PRs and international students under the MOE Tuition Grant Scheme.
The three-year MOE Tuition Grant bond must be served in a Singapore entity after graduation; under MOE Tuition Grant terms the bond may be commuted or repaid in cash.
The scholarship is only valid if an international student or Singapore PR takes up the Ministry of Education tuition grant.
If the scholarship holder changes the programme indicated in the offer, the scholarship offer may be withdrawn.
Allowances are paid for Semester 1 and Semester 2 only and do not cover vacation or special terms; students on an approved exchange during Semester 1 or 2 continue to receive the allowance.
supplements_or_initiatives: NTU-University Scholars Programme benefits: a semester abroad at a partner university, the Travel Overseas Programme for Scholars (TOPS) for Year 1 NTU-USP scholars, and an elective with a travel component.
Enrolment into the NTU Honours College, NTU's flagship undergraduate college.
Access to international symposiums and ministerial dialogues, student ambassador and student club leadership opportunities, and one-to-one faculty mentorship.
Guaranteed hall stay (online hall application required).
The scholarship may not be held concurrently with other scholarships, bursaries, university loans or awards without University approval, so it cannot be combined with other NTU awards.

Other NTU freshmen scholarships considered in the same single application include the NTU President Award, Nanyang Merit Scholarship, ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship and programme-specific awards such as the Renaissance Engineering Programme Scholarship and CN Yang Scholars Programme Scholarship; applicants may select all categories they wish to be considered for and are offered the best eligible scholarship.

programme_detail_official.description: The NTU-University Scholars Programme (NTU-USP) Scholarship is awarded to outstanding freshmen pursuing the NTU-University Scholars Programme, a multidisciplinary Signature Programme of the NTU Honours College. It is open to all nationalities and provides full coverage of subsidised tuition fees after the Tuition Grant, a living allowance of S$6,500 per academic year, an accommodation allowance of up to S$2,000 per academic year for hostel residents, a one-off computer allowance of S$2,000, and a travel grant of up to S$8,000 for an overseas study or attachment. The award carries no bond of its own beyond the three-year MOE Tuition Grant bond for Singapore PRs and international students, and requires a minimum CGPA of 3.5 over 5.0 reviewed each semester.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Subsidised tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant; living allowance, on-campus accommodation allowance, one-off computer allowance, overseas travel grant, and NTU-USP overseas-semester benefits; no coverage of the differential to the non-subsidised tuition fee.

application_readiness_checklist: Complete the NTU undergraduate admission application first; the scholarship form only opens after admission is submitted, and NTU will not process incomplete or inaccurate applications.

Confirm your own qualification route and its closing date before assuming 19 March 2027 applies to you: NUS High School Diploma closes 20 January 2027, a Singapore polytechnic diploma closes 21 February 2027, and several Year 12 equivalent routes close on 20 January 2027.
Secure admission to the NTU-University Scholars Programme itself, not only to a degree programme; the scholarship is tenable only on NTU-USP.
Draft the Personal Essay to 250 words or fewer on the compulsory topic, and order your top three achievements from the last five years in merit order before opening the form.

Brief a school teacher to be your referee in advance and send them the referee URL with your NTU application number and date of birth as soon as you submit; they have only 7 days and only one appraisal can be submitted per application.
Prepare the passport-size photograph as a digital image before you start.
Keep your email under close review from March to May, since shortlisted-only interview invitations are issued at short notice in that window.
Plan for the MOE Tuition Grant if you are an international student or Singapore PR: the scholarship is only valid if you take it up, and it carries a three-year bond.
common_rejection_risks: Assuming 19 March 2027 is your deadline when your qualification route closes on 20 January 2027 or 21 February 2027; NTU states applications submitted after the closing date will not be considered.
Applying for the scholarship before completing the admission application, which blocks the scholarship form.
Submitting an incomplete or inaccurate application, which NTU states will not be processed.
Failing to secure admission to the NTU-University Scholars Programme itself, which is the tenability condition for this award.
A late referee appraisal: only one appraisal may be submitted, and the referee has 7 days from the scholarship application.
A Personal Essay that exceeds 250 words or does not answer the single compulsory topic.
Using a family member or relative as the referee, which the terms prohibit.
Accepting another scholarship concurrently, which is prohibited without University approval; only one scholarship may be held at a time.
Changing to a different programme after receiving the offer, which can cause the scholarship offer to be withdrawn.
Dropping below a CGPA of 3.5 over 5.0 at any semester review.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The shortfall between the subsidised tuition fee and the non-subsidised tuition fee, which the award does not cover.
The portion of NTU hostel charges above the S$2,000 per academic year accommodation allowance.
Tuition or programme fees for short-term programmes outside Semester 1 and Semester 2, which NTU states are not covered by the scholarship.
Meals, transport, personal expenses and other living costs beyond the S$6,500 per academic year living allowance.
Travel costs beyond the up to S$8,000 travel grant for the overseas study or attachment programme.
Student association, hall and activity fees not covered by an allowance, plus equipment or software beyond the S$2,000 one-off computer allowance.
Repayment with interest of disbursed funds if the scholarship is withdrawn after matriculation.
document_audit: Admission application completed before the scholarship application; NTU does not process incomplete applications.
Personal Essay within the 250-word limit, answering the one compulsory topic rather than a topic of your own.
Top three personal achievements listed in clear merit order, drawn from within the last five years.
Passport-size photograph uploaded as a digital image, current and correctly named.
Referee is a school teacher or tutor and is not a family member or relative, and has been given the NTU application number and date of birth.
Referee URL forwarded promptly, with a tracked 7-day deadline (notify the referee to submit within 2 weeks at the latest).
For Year 12 equivalent applicants, the assigned application number is to hand for https://wis.ntu.edu.sg/pls/webexe/adm_fore_appl.login.
Email monitored for the interview invitation; shortlisted applicants are notified by email only, and those not shortlisted receive no email.
Only one appraisal submitted, since a second cannot be used to support the application.

alerts.message: NTU ties the scholarship deadline to the admission deadline for each qualification route, so 19 March 2027 applies only to the Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level and IB Diploma routes. The NUS High School Diploma route closes 20 January 2027, the Singapore polytechnic diploma route closes 21 February 2027, and several Year 12 equivalent routes close on 20 January 2027. Confirm your route on the NTU important dates page before relying on any date recorded here.

Although NTU states no bond is attached to the NTU-USP Scholarship apart from the MOE Tuition Grant Scheme, international students and Singapore Permanent Residents who take up the MOE Tuition Grant must work in a Singapore entity for three years after graduation. NTU states the scholarship is only valid if the Tuition Grant is taken up, so this bond is unavoidable for non-Singapore-citizen awardees.

The scholarship application is not automatic on admission. You must complete the admission application first, then submit the scholarship application in the same sitting or immediately after, using the 'Apply for Scholarship' link. A scholarship application cannot be processed without the admission application.

This scholarship is tied to enrolment on the NTU-University Scholars Programme. If you change your programme after receiving the offer, NTU states your scholarship offer can be withdrawn. NTU also states the scholarship application is distinct from the signature programme application, so submit both.

The accommodation allowance of up to S$2,000 per academic year applies only to scholarship holders who reside in NTU hostels. If you live off campus, budget the full rent yourself, though NTU guarantees a hall stay subject to an online hall application.

NTU states scholarships do not cover vacation periods or special terms, and fees for programmes outside Semesters 1 and 2 (such as GEM Discoverer) are not covered. Allowances continue only during an approved Semester 1 or 2 exchange, not during a vacation.

submission_workflow: Step 1 - Check the NTU important dates page and record the closing date for your own qualification route, plus the linked photograph and appraisal form date.
Step 2 - Complete and submit the NTU undergraduate admission application, and keep a record of the application number and password.

Step 3 - Open the 'Apply for Scholarship' link at the end of the admission application (or log in at the NTU scholarship portal, or at the Year 12 form if you hold a Year 12 equivalent qualification) using that application number.
Step 4 - Select the scholarship categories you want to be considered for; there are no restrictions on how many you select, and NTU will consider you for the best eligible scholarship.
Step 5 - List your top three personal achievements in merit order, then write the 250-word Personal Essay on the compulsory topic, and submit.
Step 6 - Upload the passport-size photograph and forward the referee URL to your school teacher with your application number and date of birth; track the 7-day referee deadline.

Step 7 - Watch for the interview invitation email (March to May for Singapore qualification routes; within 2 months of the programme offer for Year 12 routes) and prepare for a short-notice interview.
Step 8 - On an offer, accept both the admission offer and the scholarship offer by the deadline in the offer letter; accept only one scholarship and decline the others.

Step 9 - Enrol on the NTU-USP, submit the online hall application to use the guaranteed hall stay, take up the MOE Tuition Grant if you are a foreign national or SPR, and maintain a CGPA of 3.5 over 5.0 each semester.

institution_check_required: The exact MOE Tuition Grant bond terms for a specific country of study and employment, and whether the bond may be commuted or repaid in cash.

The published amount of the non-subsidised tuition fee differential, because NTU publishes only subsidised tuition fees and the amount of any shortfall depends on the applicant's nationality and degree programme.
The current NTU hostel room rates, to confirm how much of the accommodation charge the up to S$2,000 per academic year accommodation allowance does not cover.
Travel Grant Form conditions, including eligible activities and funding cap mechanics for cohorts from AY2025.
Whether the AY2027-entry benefit figures will remain unchanged, since the brochure states information is correct as at August 2026.
The NTU-USP partner university list and NTU exchange partner terms for the study-abroad semester.
Whether an accommodation allowance applies for overseas exchange semesters.
unverified_or_removed_claims: No English-language test requirement is recorded (english_requirement is null) because the NTU-USP Scholarship award page publishes none; the IELTS Academic 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 90 scores published on NTU's general admission requirements page are admission entry requirements for applicants from selected high school qualifications, not scholarship requirements, and are recorded only in english_requirement_note.
No selection weighting is recorded (selection_weighting is null) because NTU publishes no scoring rubric for this scholarship.
research_requirement is null because NTU publishes no research requirement for the NTU-USP Scholarship.

funding_amount is recorded as S$6,500 per academic year, the published living allowance and the single largest recurring published amount. NTU publishes no single headline 'total award value' figure for this scholarship, so no aggregate total has been estimated.

The 'Nanyang President's Undergraduate Scholarship' named in the research brief does not exist as a current award name on ntu.edu.sg - a direct probe of that detail-page slug returns HTTP 404, and no ntu.edu.sg page states that this award was renamed. NTU currently publishes the 'NTU President Award', whose eligibility criteria match that description (open to all nationalities; full-time undergraduate degree programme; outstanding Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, Singapore polytechnic diploma, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent qualifications; excellent co-curricular records; exceptional leadership qualities) and which the AY2026-27 NTU Scholarships brochure marks as a 'New Award'. It is therefore INFERRED, not verified, that the NTU President Award is the successor of the 'Nanyang President's Undergraduate Scholarship'. NTU publishes different benefits for it (a one-off study allowance of S$10,000, fully subsidised 4-year NTU hostel guarantee, plus support in the form of an overseas travel allowance of up to S$10,000, tuition fee coverage via bursaries and an annual study allowance of S$10,000 only where further financial aid is required - no full subsidised tuition coverage as standard). Because only one record can be written for this slot, the NTU-University Scholars Programme (NTU-USP) Scholarship, the primary named target, was recorded. The NTU President Award remains an open candidate for a separate record.
The award tenure is 'up to the normal programme duration' rather than a fixed number of years, so no single year count is recorded as duration.
Interview dates are published only as a window (between March and May, or within 2 months of the programme offer for Year 12 routes), so no exact interview date is recorded.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: The NTU-USP Scholarship award page states 'Successful awardees should be on the NTU-University Scholars Programme (NTU-USP)' and lists eligibility by pre-university qualification route (Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, Diploma awarded by a polytechnic in Singapore, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma, Year 12 equivalent), which are undergraduate entry qualifications. The NTU Scholarships brochure lists this award on page 10 under 'Type of Scholarship' = 'Freshmen-Signature Programme' and 'Programme' = 'On the NTU-University Scholars Programme (NTU-USP)', and the NTU-USP programme page states NTU-USP is 'a benefit-restricted interdisciplinary undergraduate programme' in which every NTU-USP scholar 'reads a full degree or double degree programme' alongside the programme. NTU's scholarship application process page states you 'should submit your online scholarship application immediately after you've completed your admission application' for undergraduate admission.
